name: TextBox 8
text: Operations Research (OR): OR is a discipline that applies advanced analytical methods, mathematical modeling, and quantitative techniques(computer programming) to solve complex decision-making problems. It seeks to optimize processes, resources, and systems. It is more about theoretical study.Operations Management (OM): OM focuses on the design, operation, and improvement of the processes involved in producing goods and services. It is more about empirical study.

name: Title 1
text: What is Operational Research (Business modelling and simulation)?

name: TextBox 3
text: The scientific approach to decision making usually involves the use of one or more mathematical models.Most classical models require many simplifying assumptions.

name: TextBox 3
text: Because of complexity, stochastic relations, and so on, not all real-world problems can be represented or solved by mathematical models and can only analyzed by simulation.Sometimes we also use simulation to validate the results of mathematical modelling.

name: TextBox 3
text: ﻿Gardening problem:﻿A homeowner is in the process of starting a backyard vegetable garden. The garden must take on a rectangular shape to facilitate row irrigation. To keep critters out, the garden must be fenced. The owner has enough material to build a fence of length L = 100 ft. The goal is to fence the largest possible rectangular area.

name: TextBox 3
text: ﻿Components of a model:Objective functionDecision variablesConstraints

name: TextBox 3
text: ﻿Components of a model:Objective function: maximize profit/minimize costDecision variables: how much to order/deliver, whether to launch production/ set up a machineConstraints: capacity/service level

name: TextBox 3
text: ﻿﻿A solution is feasible if it satisfies all the constraints, otherwise unfeasible. ﻿ A solution is optimal if, in addition to being feasible, it yields the best (maximum or minimum) value of the objective function.

name: TextBox 3
text: ﻿﻿﻿The decision variables in the objectives and constraints are always multiplied by constants and added together. Such a model is a linear model.﻿ If an optimization model is not linear, then it is a nonlinear model.

name: TextBox 3
text: ﻿﻿﻿﻿If one or more decision variables must be integer, then we say that an optimization model is an integer model.﻿ If all the decision variables are free to assume fractional values, then the optimization model is a noninteger model.

name: TextBox 3
text: ﻿All the parameters are known. We then have a deterministic model.﻿ Non-deterministic model a stochastic model. (There are usually some stochastic parameters in the model)

name: TextBox 3
text: ﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿A static model is one in which the decision variables do not involve sequences of decisions over multiple periods.﻿A dynamic model is a model in which the decision variables do involve sequences of decisions over multiple periods.

When a production order is issued to the production department, necessary raw materials are acquired from the company’s stocks or purchased from outside sources. name: 矩形: 圆角 5
text: Solutions are rooted in people and not in technology

name: TextBox 3
text: ﻿Travelers arriving at the Intercontinental Airport in Houston, Texas, complained about the long wait for their baggage. Authorities increased the number of ﻿baggage handlers in hope of alleviating the problem, but the complaints persisted.

name: TextBox 9
text: In the end, the decision was made to simply move arrival gates farther away from baggage claim, forcing the passengers to walk longer before reaching the baggage area. The complaints disappeared because the extra walking allowed ample time for the luggage to be delivered to the carousel.

name: TextBox 3
text: ﻿﻿In response to complaints of slow elevator service in a large office building, the OR team initially perceived the situation as a waiting-line problem that might require the use of mathematical queuing analysis or simulation.

name: TextBox 7
text: After studying the behavior of the people voicing the complaint, the psychologist on the team suggested installing full-length mirrors at the entrance to the elevators. The complaints disappeared, as people were kept occupied watching themselves and others while waiting for the elevator.

name: TextBox 3
text: Severalf departments in a production facility share the use of three trucks to transport material. Requests initiated by a department are filled on a first-come first-serve basis. Nevertheless, the departments complained of long wait for service and demanded adding a fourth truck to the pool. Further investigations revealed that the trucks were parked in an obscure parking lot out of the line of vision for the departments. A requesting supervisor, lacking visual sighting ofthe trucks, assumed that no trucks were available and hence did not initiate a request. ﻿

name: TextBox 7
text: The problem was solved simply by installing two-way radio communication between the truck lot and each department.
